title: The Ridge Where Paddocks Grow Steep

features.name: performance marker
features.desc-on-touch: A stone with worn lines: people have walked here and pretended to remember. Each year a group returns to act out a past that shifts slightly. The grass holds the shapes of multiple stories.

features.name: local roster
features.desc-on-touch: Names carved into wood and kept updated. Not the dead — the people who walked here and spoke the ridge into a different shape. The roster contradicts itself by region; the park knows more versions of itself than any history can hold.

features.name: terrain memory
features.desc-on-touch: The ridge's own archive: how many times the paddock reshaped itself, how many years the game was played, how many stories the same landscape held. The earth here is a text that rewrites each season.

features.name: elevation gate
features.desc-on-touch: Where the paddock steepens and the flatland says goodbye. Beyond here, memory becomes choreography. The climb is always the same route, but each person walks it as a different story.

features.name: shadow map
features.desc-on-touch: A drawing in the dirt: all the overlapping paths people have taken up this ridge. No single trail — instead a density, a heatmap of footfalls. The shadow shows how many people played the same place as different people.

inscription: the paddock reshapes itself each year; by season's end the story has changed the land

file.name: Ridge_Performance_Overlays_Handwritten.txt
file.note: Notes on group stagings here across decades. Archive holds multiple versions of the same walk. The landscape contradicts itself and holds both versions as true.

reverie.title: REVERIE — high paddock at turning time
narr: You both walk the ridge as others have walked it. The game
is to pretend the first time. The slope rises like it knows
you're keeping a story that isn't finished. She says:
"What if we both played different endings?" and the earth
holds the question. The paddock will reshape itself. You'll
both leave, and it will still remember you chose to stay.
